findings.message: GC advances lastCheckpointGC before collection runs, including attempts that fail to list resources or delete checkpoints. Subsequent maintenance calls skip collection until the GC interval elapses. Restore error propagation and update lastCheckpointGC only after successful collection so failures remain eligible for retry.
findings.evidence: recommender.go:158–160 checks the interval, assigns lastCheckpointGC, then invokes collection. cluster_feeder.go:289 returns no result; listing failures log and return at 294–297 and 307–310, while deletion failures log and continue at 323–325.

findings.message: Checkpoint writing and GC share a deadline started before writing. If writing consumes that budget, GC starts with an expired context; even shorter writes reduce its available time. Restore independently started timeout contexts derived from the parent, with GC's timeout starting when collection begins.
findings.evidence: recommender.go:190–192 creates one deadline using checkpointsWriteTimeout and passes it to MaintainCheckpoints. Lines 156 and 160 pass the same context sequentially to writing and GC. cluster_feeder.go:323 passes that context to checkpoint deletion. The diff removes the independent write and GC timeout contexts and GC timeout configuration.

result.coverage: Verified both existing findings against the supplied diff and numbered source excerpts, limited to checkpoint GC success tracking and timeout ownership. No whole-repository completeness claim.
limitations: No tools were used, files read, or tests run.
Checkpoint writer and deletion client implementations were not supplied, so exact cancellation behavior and downstream operational impact are unverified.
result.contribution: Preserved both distinct supported defects. Qualified the second finding by replacing the unconditional claim that cleanup cannot delete checkpoints with the directly supported expired-context and reduced-budget behavior. No findings were removed or added.
